c1b60df422ad7bec: KUALA LUMPUR: The government's move to offer permanent positions to more than 9,000 contract doctors under the 2027 Budget has prompted calls for similar clarity on the future of contract pharmacists, who continue to face employment uncertainty.
The Malaysian Pharmacists Society (MPS) said contract pharmacists should not be overlooked in efforts to address longstanding job insecurity in the public healthcare sector.

Its president, Professor Amrahi Buang, welcomed the government's announcement but said pharmacists who had served for years in public hospitals, health clinics and other Health Ministry facilities also deserved a clear pathway to permanent employment.
"Pharmacists who have committed years of service to the public healthcare system deserve a transparent, fair and sustainable pathway towards long-term employment.
"A solution to the contract healthcare workforce issue cannot be considered complete if pharmacists facing the same employment uncertainty are left without a clear pathway forward.

"This is not a call for preferential treatment. It is a call for fairness, transparency and appropriate recognition of every healthcare profession that contributes to the delivery of public healthcare," he said in a statement today.

Amrahi said many contract pharmacists continued to face uncertainty over permanent appointments, career progression and their long-term future, despite playing essential roles in medication management, clinical pharmacy services, medication safety and antimicrobial stewardship.

He called on the government and Health Ministry to clarify their plans for contract pharmacists, including those still serving, those on reserve lists and those who had completed their contractual service.

MPS also called for a transparent timeline and mechanism for permanent appointments, alongside meaningful engagement with the profession to determine the ministry's long-term pharmacy workforce requirements.

Amrahi acknowledged that workforce requirements and appointment mechanisms differed between healthcare professions, but said this should not leave contract pharmacists without clarity over their future indefinitely.

When tabling the 2027 Budget, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced that more than 9,000 contract doctors would be offered permanent positions next year. This follows the appointment of more than 15,000 contract doctors to permanent positions since 2023, including 4,000 this year.

Anwar also announced that the monthly post-basic incentive for 47,000 paramedics and nurses would increase from RM100 to RM200. The Health Ministry's allocation will rise to RM47.7 billion next year, from RM46.5 billion this year.
ee152f423e79b836: PETALING JAYA: Komitmen kerajaan untuk menamatkan sistem doktor kontrak perlu disusuli pelaksanaan berkesan, proses telus dan hasil yang dapat dirasai pegawai perubatan, kata kumpulan yang memperjuangkan isu berkenaan.

Hartal Doktor Kontrak (HDK) berkata pengumuman Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim ketika membentangkan Belanjawan 2027 hari ini menandakan titik perubahan penting buat warga perubatan selepas hampir sedekad berdepan ketidakpastian kerjaya.
Katanya, sejak sistem itu diperkenalkan pada 2016, ribuan doktor mengharungi ketidakjaminan masa depan serta peluang kemajuan kerjaya yang tidak seimbang.
"Bagi mereka yang sekian lama memperjuangkan perubahan, pengumuman ini hadir sebagai sinar harapan yang telah lama dinantikan," menurut kenyataan.
Anwar hari ini mengumumkan lebih 9,000 doktor kontrak akan ditawarkan jawatan tetap pada tahun depan.
Tambahnya, doktor yang berjaya menamatkan latihan siswazah selepas ini akan ditawarkan jawatan tetap sebagai pegawai perubatan.
HDK merakamkan penghargaan kepada Anwar dan kerajaan atas komitmen untuk menangani isu yang sekian lama membebani profesion perubatan.

Bagaimanapun, garis masa pelaksanaan yang jelas, kriteria kelayakan yang adil serta pengiktirafan sewajarnya terhadap doktor yang telah bertahun-tahun berkhidmat secara kontrak penting bagi memastikan tiada keciciran.

"Penamatan sistem doktor kontrak juga perlu menjadi sebahagian daripada usaha lebih menyeluruh untuk menambah baik keadaan kerja, memperkukuh laluan kemajuan kerjaya dan mengekalkan doktor berpengalaman dalam sistem penjagaan kesihatan awam negara," katanya.
HDK menyambut baik komitmen berkenaan dengan harapan berhati-hati, dan akan terus menuntut kebertanggungjawaban bagi memastikan perubahan dilaksanakan sepenuhnya.
Katanya, selepas 10 tahun menanti, doktor berhak mendapat lebih daripada sekadar janji, sebaliknya sistem yang menjamin keadilan, kestabilan kerjaya dan maruah profesion.
"Pengumuman ini telah menyemarakkan harapan. Kini, pelaksanaanlah yang harus membuktikan makna sebenar harapan tersebut," katanya.
27f653b8bc6df314: BANGKOK: A Thai court on Friday dismissed a challenge by a Chinese investigative journalist over his prolonged detention in Bangkok, a day after authorities began proceedings to extradite him to China, his lawyer said.
Bai Zhaodong, who is recognised by the United Nations as a refugee, left China in 2023 and arrived the following year in Thailand.
The 56-year-old had been detained at a Bangkok immigration centre since January, and he earlier filed a petition against what he said was unlawful detention by Thai immigration authorities.
On Thursday, Thai prosecutors arrested Bai under an extradition warrant issued by Beijing and moved him to a remand prison.
At a hearing on Friday morning, which was scheduled weeks earlier, Bangkok South Criminal Court rejected Bai's challenge against his detention, according to his lawyer.
"Because there is an extradition request from China saying he is wanted in China, the (court ruled that) detention is necessary," Nadthasiri Bergman told AFP.
Bai was not in court on Friday but is expected to appear at a Jan 25 hearing in the extradition case.
China's foreign ministry said in July that Bai was suspected of extortion and bribery, and an extradition request had been submitted to Thailand.

Bergman said the Chinese embassy in Bangkok sent a letter to the Thai Immigration Office in June 2025 asking to extradite Bai, while an official request dated March 4, was sent to the Office of the Attorney General.
Rights campaigners believe Bai's life could be at risk if he is returned to China, saying he faced growing persecution over two decades of work exposing government corruption.

An undisclosed third country has offered Bai asylum but two attempts to travel there were cancelled this year after Thai immigration authorities withheld exit clearance without explanation, his legal team says.
Reporters Without Borders has called his treatment "scandalous" while Maya Wang, deputy Asia director at Human Rights Watch, said the move to extradite Bai was "deeply troubling."
"Thailand should not succumb to pressure from Beijing to extradite Bai based on trumped up charges," she said.
- HAVEN FOR FUGITIVES -
Beijing has long sought to clamp down on dissidents overseas, and campaigners accuse authorities in Thailand – where several notable activists have moved over the years – of complicity.

Thailand is not a party to the UN Refugee Convention, but is bound by the international legal principle of non-refoulement, which bars countries from sending people back to places where their lives or freedom are in danger.
Nonetheless Bangkok deported 40 Uyghurs to China in February last year over the objections of activists, who said the men could be tortured or mistreated.
The Thai foreign ministry did not respond to an AFP request for comment.
Questioned by AFP at a regular briefing Friday, Chinese foreign affairs ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning urged all countries to cooperate in "eliminating lawless areas and safe havens for fugitives."

"China's judicial organs handle cases in strict accordance with the law, carry out law enforcement and judicial cooperation with relevant countries in accordance with the law and agreements, and fully safeguard the lawful rights of relevant parties," she said.--AFP

49e2535ecbb600c4: BENGALURU: Elise Mertens stunned former champion Iga Swiatek 7-6(0) 6-3 on Friday to reach the China Open semi-finals, continuing her impressive run in Beijing after also eliminating American third seed Coco Gauff earlier in the week.

The 30-year-old Belgian, ranked 19th in the world, produced a composed display to secure back-to-back victories over Grand Slam champions and advance to just the third WTA 1000 semi-final of her career and her first since 2021.

Mertens seized control by dominating the opening-set tiebreak without dropping a point and carried that momentum into the second set, breaking Swiatek and completing one of the biggest upsets of the tournament.
She will next face home favourite Zheng Qinwen, who defeated sixth seed Elina Svitolina 6-3 7-6(6) earlier in the day to book her place in the last four.

Playing on a wildcard, Zheng took charge early by breaking Svitolina three times in the opening set. The Ukrainian world number seven responded strongly in the second, raising her level to force a tiebreak.
Zheng recovered from a sluggish start in the breaker, reeling off four consecutive points to regain the initiative before sealing victory in one hour and 47 minutes.
Svitolina competed well throughout but was unable to withstand Zheng's attacking game as the Olympic champion consistently forced the pace and seized the initiative in crucial moments.
"I'm just happy to have a lot of winners during the match, and at the end, be brave in important moments," Zheng told reporters.
The victory took Zheng to her fourth career WTA 1000 semi-final and her third on Chinese soil, following appearances in Beijing and Wuhan in 2024.
799aa6c4087e00d9: PETALING JAYA: Bank Negara Malaysia's (BNM) additional RM5 billion allocation for the Small and Medium Enterprise Stabilisation Relief Facility is expected to benefit 9,000 more SMEs, including microenterprises.
The facility will provide access to affordable working capital, Bernama reported.

The central bank said the additional relief will also help SMEs manage temporary cash-flow pressures, maintain operations, and strengthen business resilience amid the economic impact of the ongoing West Asia conflict.
"As at Sept 30, 2026, RM3.8 billion in financing under the facility’s initial RM5 billion allocation has been approved, benefitting more than 6,800 SME accounts," BNM said in a statement today.
It added that the financing facility will remain available to affected SMEs across all economic sectors until June 30, 2027, or full utilisation, whichever is earlier.

Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, who is also the finance minister, said during the tabling of the 2027 budget today that BNM had agreed to add another RM5 billion to support SMEs affected by the conflict.

On the implementation of the Cakna funding initiative to help micro, small and medium enterprises, BNM said it would be strengthened further to expand access to working capital for small contractors (G1-G4) undertaking government projects and help support the timely completion of projects.
"To further reduce financing costs, the RM10 nominal stamp duty treatment for Cakna I and II financing agreements will also be extended until Dec 31, 2030," it said.
134756c18fdcdbe1: KUALA LUMPUR: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi arrived at the Bunga Raya Complex at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) about 6.20pm today to begin a 2-day state visit to Malaysia.
He was received by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin.
El-Sisi is visiting Malaysia at the invitation of Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim.
In a Facebook post, Anwar welcomed El-Sisi and said he had headed to the Bunga Raya Complex after tabling the 2027 Budget to receive the Egyptian president.

46f5355b2e1d33ad: PETALING JAYA: Anggaran RM460 bilion bagi perbelanjaan tahun depan merupakan belanjawan terbesar setakat ini, melonjak hampir 10% berbanding unjuran 2026. Daripada jumlah tersebut, kira-kira RM83 bilion diperuntukkan bagi perbelanjaan pembangunan, manakala RM377 bilion disalurkan untuk menampung perbelanjaan mengurus.
Ketika membentangkan Belanjawan 2027, Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim menegaskan kos sara hidup menjadi keutamaan memandangkan ia 'isu utama yang membebankan rakyat'.

Bagi menangani cabaran itu, beliau mengumumkan pelbagai program sokongan merangkumi RM80 bilion dalam bentuk bantuan tunai, subsidi serta insentif, selain pelepasan cukai khusus untuk golongan berpendapatan sederhana.

Dari segi agihan sektor, Kementerian Pendidikan (KPM) sekali lagi mendahului senarai penerima peruntukan terbesar dengan RM69 bilion, disusuli Kementerian Kesihatan (KKM) yang menerima hampir RM48 bilion, manakala Kementerian Pertahanan serta Kementerian Dalam Negeri masing-masing diperuntukkan RM22 bilion.

Peruntukan bagi sektor pendidikan merangkumi RM2 bilion untuk kerja pembaikan dan penyelenggaraan sekolah, dengan hampir RM1.3 bilion dikhususkan bagi menaik taraf 682 sekolah daif terutamanya di Sabah dan Sarawak. Sekolah kebangsaan pula akan menerima RM900 juta, manakala sekolah jenis kebangsaan Cina (SJKC) diperuntukkan RM100 juta dan sekolah jenis kebangsaan Tamil (SJKT) sebanyak RM50 juta.
Inti pati utama Belanjawan 2027:
Penjawat awam, pesara
Seramai 1.3 juta penjawat awam Gred Utama B dan ke bawah, termasuk lantikan kontrak, akan menerima bantuan khas kewangan sebanyak RM1,500.
Lebih sejuta pesara kerajaan, merangkumi veteran berpencen serta tidak berpencen, masing-masing akan menerima RM750.
Kadar pencen bulanan minimum pula dinaikkan daripada RM1,000 kepada RM1,350, sekali gus memanfaatkan hampir 59,000 pesara, veteran tentera, serta penerima pencen terbitan.
Subsidi dan bantuan
Lebih RM80 bilion diperuntukkan bagi subsidi, bantuan, dan insentif sepanjang 2027, dengan subsidi bahan api kekal tinggi pada unjuran RM40 bilion.

Bantuan Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) sehingga RM150 sebulan akan disalurkan kepada sembilan juta penerima. Selain itu, rakyat Malaysia berusia 18 tahun ke atas turut menerima bantuan SARA RM100 sebanyak dua kali yang akan memberi manfaat kepada kira-kira 13 juta individu.
Gaji minimum naik ke RM2,000
Gaji minimum dinaikkan daripada RM1,700 kepada RM2,000 bermula Jun tahun depan yang memanfaatkan lebih empat juta pekerja.
Bagaimanapun, perusahaan mikro, kecil dan sederhana (PMKS) dengan jualan tahunan bawah RM50 juta dikecualikan daripada kenaikan itu bagi memberi ruang penyesuaian model perniagaan mereka.

Gaji permulaan minimum RM2,500 sebulan turut diperkenalkan untuk pekerja separa mahir dan graduan, manakala penanda aras gaji kehidupan wajar dinaikkan daripada RM3,100 kepada RM3,400 sebulan bagi manfaat 230,000 pekerja.
Potongan, pelepasan cukai pendapatan
Had pelepasan cukai pendapatan individu dinaikkan daripada RM9,000 kepada RM12,000.

Pelepasan cukai turut diperluas merangkumi skop perbelanjaan lebih luas, termasuk penjagaan selepas bersalin, penjagaan ibu bapa serta datuk dan nenek, pendidikan dan latihan kemahiran, serta langganan kecerdasan buatan (AI).

Kadar cukai bagi pendapatan bercukai antara RM70,000 hingga RM100,000 diturunkan kepada 18% berbanding 19%, manakala kadar bagi pendapatan antara RM100,000 hingga RM150,000 dikurangkan kepada 24% daripada 25%.
Bagi individu berpendapatan melebihi RM1 juta setahun, kadar cukai dinaikkan kepada 30%.
Kadar cukai PMKS diturunkan
Kadar cukai bagi PMKS dikurangkan satu mata peratusan tahun depan.

Menerusi Belanjawan 2027, kadar cukai ke atas RM150,000 pertama pendapatan bercukai diturunkan kepada 14%, manakala kadar bagi pendapatan bercukai antara RM150,000 hingga RM600,000 pula dipotong kepada 16%.
Kawal selia e-dagang

Rang Undang-Undang (RUU) E-Dagang akan dibentangkan pada sidang Parlimen akan datang bagi memperkukuh akauntabiliti platform serta penjual dalam talian, mengekang persaingan tidak adil daripada pengendali e-dagang asing yang tidak dikawal selia, dan melindungi PMKS tempatan.
Pengangkutan dan perjalanan pelajar
Pas baharu MyKomuter50 akan diperkenalkan untuk pengguna KTM Komuter, yang dijangka memberi penjimatan sehingga RM160 sebulan kepada penumpang.
Pas perjalanan percuma pula akan disediakan kepada 360,000 murid sekolah, orang kurang upaya (OKU), serta kanak-kanak berusia bawah enam tahun.
Subsidi tiket penerbangan FlySiswa Madani untuk penuntut universiti dinaikkan daripada RM400 kepada RM500, memberi manfaat kepada lebih 60,000 mahasiswa universiti awam.
Lebih banyak jawatan tetap untuk doktor kontrak

Lebih 9,000 doktor kontrak dalam perkhidmatan kesihatan awam akan ditawarkan jawatan tetap tahun depan. Graduan yang menamatkan pengajian perubatan pula akan terus ditawarkan pelantikan tetap sebagai pegawai perubatan.
Kadar elaun pos bagi paramedik dan jururawat dinaikkan sekali ganda kepada RM200 sebulan berbanding RM100 sebelum ini.
Bagi mengekang manipulasi harga, hospital swasta akan mengguna pakai kategori pengebilan yang diselaraskan bermula 2027.
Insurans perubatan mampu milik
Pelan insurans dan takaful perubatan asas mampu milik kerajaan, MediAsas, akan dilancarkan pada Januari.
Pelan ini menetapkan caj hospital yang diselaraskan mengikut diagnosis dan jenis rawatan, sekali gus menjadikan kos perubatan lebih mudah dijangka dan diurus.
Tangguh bayaran balik PTPTN
Kerajaan akan menangguhkan bayaran balik pinjaman Perbadanan Tabung Pendidikan Tinggi Nasional (PTPTN) pada 2027 bagi peminjam berpendapatan bulanan RM2,500 ke bawah.
Bagi peminjam berpendapatan antara RM2,500 hingga RM3,000 sebulan, mereka hanya perlu membuat bayaran balik minimum RM50 sebulan.
Langkah berkenaan dijangka memberi manfaat kepada lebih 400,000 peminjam PTPTN.
a5907c1af613252b: PETALING JAYA: The Federation of Malaysian Manufacturing has expressed disappointment with the 2027 budget, saying it lacks support for the manufacturing sector.
FMM president Jacob Lee said the manufacturing industry was struggling with rising operating costs as well as barriers to technology adoption, innovation and green investments.

Lee said FMM was disappointed that its proposed RM1.5 billion support package was not adopted for the federal budget. "This leaves a gap in dedicated grant support to help manufacturing small and medium-sized enterprises meet technology adoption costs," he said in a statement.
Lee urged the finance ministry to consult the industry on the proposed minimum wage of RM2,500 per month for semi-skilled workers and graduates.
The wage should be driven by the market and not set by the government, he said. It should reflect job requirements while demonstrating the competence and productivity of the workers.

"Existing skills mismatches mean employers may face both higher wage obligations and additional training costs to equip recruits with the capabilities required for their roles. FMM therefore calls for industry consultation on the proposed framework."

However, Lee welcomed the review of the reinvestment allowance, expressing hope for a clearer eligibility criteria and greater accessibility. The allowance would encourage manufacturers to reinvest in automation and technology, which is key to boosting competitiveness and creating higher-value jobs, he said.
He also welcomed plans to enact a law to better regulate e-commerce platforms, particularly due to foreign firms entering the local market without proper oversight and enforcement.
Lee said Putrajaya should review the impact of low-priced imports entering Malaysia through conventional and online trade channels.

"The proposed E-Commerce Bill should be complemented by a comprehensive review of existing trade and regulatory measures, with appropriate safeguards against unfair trade practices, underpriced imports and non-compliant products," he said. "The objective should be to ensure a level playing field for Malaysian manufacturers and SMEs without restricting legitimate trade or consumer choice."

3d77e0617921f657: BEIJING: China and the European Union reached an "understanding" on hybrid vehicles on Friday, as their commerce chiefs concluded talks with an agreement to strengthen dialogue, dispelling fears of a full-blown trade war.

The EU's Maros Sefcovic and China's Wang Wentao agreed both sides would adhere to "procedures concerning company price undertakings" of hybrid cars, Beijing's commerce ministry said, citing a joint statement.
The critical automotive sector was a focal point in the lead-up to talks, as cheaper products coming from China have strangled European industry and Brussels has sought to manage those exports.
In a move that will bring further relief to Brussels, Beijing also committed to continuing the supply of vital items such as rare earth minerals to the European Union.
China is "willing... to continue facilitating the approval of export licenses for rare earths and permanent magnets destined for the EU", the statement said.
While they acknowledged "differences" between them, the two sides were committed to maintaining trade and to hold a further meeting in March.
The talks follow months of rising tensions between the 27-nation EU and the Asian powerhouse that threatened to escalate into a trade war.
Sefcovic had said it was "crucial" that the talks deliver "tangible outcomes", after he met with Wang on Thursday.
He said earlier in the day that the EU's trade deficit with China, running at around one billion euros ($1.1 billion) every day, was "unsustainable".
Many in Europe accuse China of unfair trade practices, including supporting firms with huge subsidies, price dumping and currency manipulation.
Europe can ill afford to anger Beijing, but the stakes are also high for China, which is heavily reliant on exports to compensate for its weak domestic economy.
The EU parliament's trade committee chief, Bernd Lange, said ahead of Sefcovic's trip that this "economic crisis in China" gives the bloc "bargaining power".
There is some "nervousness" during the talks among members of the European Union Chamber of Commerce in China, according to Adam Dunnett, the lobby's secretary general.
European companies with local operations "recognise the importance and the real issue of the outstanding trade imbalance", Dunnett told AFP on Friday in Beijing.
"They fully support that that needs to be addressed, but they want it to be done in a proportionate, specific and negotiated way so that we can manage the overall relationship," he said.

Beijing's commitment to continue providing rare earths will bring some comfort to European companies in China, who face complicated access to the critical materials under new rules imposed by Beijing last year in retaliation against tariffs announced by US President Donald Trump.
"Having a bit more transparency and predictability around that" is a key deliverable from this week's talks, he said.
ff700f5903e44611: PETALING JAYA: Businesses should not use the increase in the minimum wage to RM2,000 as an excuse to raise the prices of goods and services unreasonably, says the Federation of Malaysian Consumers Associations.
Fomca chief executive T Saravanan said the government must monitor prices to ensure rising living costs do not offset the benefits of the wage increase.
He said Fomca supported the government’s move to raise the minimum wage from RM1,700 to RM2,000 a month, as it would boost workers' purchasing power.
However, the government should provide further details on which categories of workers and employers would be subject to the new rate, including the exemption criteria for small businesses.
“The government must monitor the possibility of unreasonable price increases for goods and services on the grounds of higher wage costs,” he told FMT.

The increase in the minimum wage, from RM1,700 to RM2,000 a month from next June was announced in the 2027 budget tabled by Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim today. It is expected to benefit more than four million workers.
However, businesses with annual sales of less than RM50 million would be exempted from the new rate to give them room to adjust their business models.
The Consumers Association of Penang described the increase to RM2,000 as an improvement but said the amount remained too low to meet workers' living expenses.

“CAP has long advocated an increase in the minimum wage, including calling for the implementation of a living wage," said CAP honorary secretary S Mageswari. "An increase in the minimum wage is necessary to ensure social and economic justice."

She said an increase in the minimum wage must be accompanied by measures to control inflation and monitor prices so that the people can enjoy its real benefits without being burdened by rising living costs.

Workers in small enterprises were equally entitled to benefit from the new minimum wage and should not continue to be left behind. She urged the government to provide additional support, including transitional assistance to help employers adjust to the wage increase.
d2c2f3409f89bbc3: PETALING JAYA: Kerajaan perlu menangani kekurangan hampir 11,000 pakar bagi memenuhi keperluan populasi menua dan peningkatan beban penyakit tidak berjangkit, kata Persatuan Perubatan Malaysia (MMA).

Presiden Dr Sivanaesan Letchumanan menggesa peluang latihan kepakaran diperluaskan, kemajuan kerjaya ditingkatkan dan pengagihan tenaga kerja di seluruh fasiliti penjagaan kesihatan awam dioptimumkan menerusi pelaburan berterusan.

MMA turut mencadangkan papan pemuka kebangsaan diwujudkan bagi pengagihan tenaga kerja penjagaan kesihatan, untuk memberikan gambaran jelas mengenai tahap penempatan petugas dan kekurangan tenaga kerja di hospital serta klinik awam, bagi memastikan sumber dimanfaatkan secara berkesan.

Menyentuh aspek penting lain dalam Belanjawan 2027 yang dibentangkan hari ini, Sivanaesan menekankan potensi kerjasama antara sektor awam dan swasta, pelaburan dalam peralatan perubatan, serta inisiatif kesihatan digital untuk memendekkan tempoh menunggu pesakit dan meningkatkan mutu perkhidmatan kesihatan secara keseluruhan, lapor Bernama.

"Pada akhirnya, Belanjawan 2027 bukan sekadar diukur berdasarkan peruntukan yang diumumkan, tetapi sejauh mana ia mampu meningkatkan mutu penjagaan pesakit, memendekkan tempoh menunggu, mengekalkan tenaga kerja kesihatan dan memperluas akses kepada perkhidmatan kesihatan," katanya.
Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim hari ini mengumumkan peruntukan kepada Kementerian Kesihatan ditingkatkan kepada RM47.7 bilion berbanding RM46.5 bilion pada 2026.

Antara langkah utama dalam sektor kesihatan ialah menyerap lebih 9,000 doktor kontrak ke jawatan tetap, meningkatkan peruntukan bagi khidmat rawatan pesakit di luar fasiliti kerajaan kepada RM200 juta, memperkenalkan skim MediAsas, menyediakan RM1.2 bilion untuk penyelenggaraan fasiliti kesihatan serta memperluas penggunaan sistem rekod perubatan elektronik.
Sivanaesan berkata jaminan pelantikan tetap kepada graduan perubatan yang selesai menjalani latihan siswazah memberikan kestabilan pekerjaan dan hala tuju kerjaya yang lebih jelas kepada doktor muda.

"Hal ini merupakan pencapaian penting yang memenuhi satu daripada tuntutan MMA sejak sekian lama. Kami menghargai usaha kerajaan ke arah menjamin kestabilan pekerjaan dan memberikan hala tuju kerjaya yang lebih jelas kepada doktor muda kita.
"Pelantikan tetap adalah satu perkembangan positif namun perlu disokong oleh strategi pengekalan tenaga kerja yang menyeluruh," katanya.

371d81e4ad94ef14: PETALING JAYA: A contract doctors’ group sees "a glimmer of hope" in the government's offer of permanent positions for more than 9,000 contract doctors in the public health service next year.

eb04a676f3408e39: The global PC market has taken a beating, with shipments plunging more than 20 percent in the third quarter as the AI-driven memory shortage pushes up prices and buyers decide their existing machines will do just fine. New figures from Omdia show worldwide shipments of desktops, notebooks, and workstations fell 21.2 percent year-on-year to 58.1 million units in Q3 2026. IDC tells a similar story, estimating a 20.1 percent decline to 62.7 million units. The research firms differ on shipment totals, but agree the market has gone from bad to considerably worse. The downturn follows a rush to buy PCs earlier this year, when manufacturers, distributors, and corporate customers brought forward orders to get ahead of anticipated price increases. That helped prop up shipments in the first half of 2026, but left the industry with a pile of inventory and fewer buyers in the third quarter. IDC said shipments fell 9.1 percent from Q2, bucking the usual seasonal pattern in which back-to-school demand lifts the PC market. "What we're seeing is the result of the strong first half pull-in," said Jitesh Ubrani, research director for consumer devices at IDC. "Vendors and channels loaded up on inventory early in the year to get ahead of price hikes, and that has thrown off the usual seasonality, where Q3 is typically larger than Q2." Much of the trouble stems from the AI industry's appetite for memory and storage, which has left PC makers competing for increasingly expensive components. The shortage was already taking its toll in Q2, when IDC initially reported a 4.9 percent decline in shipments, since revised to 3.8 percent. Omdia estimates that DRAM and SSDs now account for nearly 40 percent of a PC's component costs, up from around 15 percent previously, following more than fourfold price increases. Shortages of processors, graphics cards, and other integrated circuits are also adding to manufacturers' woes. The damage is being felt across the industry's biggest names. Lenovo retained its position as the world's largest PC vendor, shipping 14.9 million units, although IDC estimates that represents a 22.6 percent decline from a year earlier. HP fared worse, with shipments plunging nearly 31 percent to 10.3 million units. Dell recorded a 25 percent drop to 7.6 million, while Apple escaped relatively lightly with an 11 percent decline, according to IDC. The Mac maker even increased its market share despite shipping fewer machines. Omdia puts Apple's shipments higher, at 6.8 million units compared with IDC's 5.9 million. Buyers may get some relief as retailers and distributors try to clear excess stock, but IDC doesn't expect a return to the prices consumers paid a year ago. "Channels are now worried about carrying too much inventory into a market where high prices are suppressing demand," Ubrani said. "That could translate into promotions and some short-term relief for consumers, but we don't expect pricing anywhere near what it was a year ago." The outlook isn't particularly cheerful. Omdia expects global PC shipments to fall another 24 percent year-on-year in the fourth quarter, followed by a further 7 percent decline across 2027. For an industry hoping AI would help sell more PCs, that's quite the result. ®

11b238dec5e62c6c: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The government is allocating RM2.62 billion in aid to paddy farmers under Budget 2027, covering various subsidies and incentives to increase rice production and safeguard their welfare.

Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the assistance would enable paddy farmers to receive benefits of about RM4,300 per hectare of paddy field, including subsidies for seeds, fertiliser, pesticides, ploughing costs and paddy prices.

He said the government had agreed to increase the paddy harvesting incentive from RM50 to RM100 per hectare per season, while the ploughing incentive, which had been increased to RM300, would be maintained and extended to paddy farmers in Sabah and Sarawak.
“To rehabilitate and rejuvenate paddy fields, RM20 million will be provided to supply foliar fertiliser for more than 10,000 hectares of paddy fields.

“The Five-Season Padi Cultivation in Two Years Project is crucial to ensuring the continuity of the country’s rice supply, and work to upgrade irrigation systems in 15 paddy field blocks is progressing according to schedule. In addition, the Pedu Dam rehabilitation project in Kedah is expected to be completed by the end of 2027,” he said when tabling Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat today.

For the fisheries and fishing sector, he said the government would increase the number of special boat licence holders from 17,000 to 20,000 fishermen, with an allocation of RM30 million, while providing aquaculture project grants and RM40 million in financing through Agrobank.

Eligible fishermen will also continue to enjoy subsidised diesel at RM1.65 per litre, while RM178 million will be allocated, among others, for catch incentives and a monthly Cost of Living Allowance of up to RM300.

Anwar said the government had allocated RM300 million to strengthen cooperation with state governments in implementing agrofood projects, in addition to providing more than RM1 billion in financing to agro-entrepreneurs through Agrobank, Bank Rakyat and the Malaysia Cooperative Societies Commission.

For smallholders in the oil palm sector, the government is providing RM100 million in hybrid financing for replanting involving 4,500 smallholders, as well as RM200 million in soft financing, with smallholders bearing only a two per cent interest rate and being granted a four-year repayment deferment.

The allocation for rehabilitating farm roads will also be doubled from RM50 million to RM100 million, while RM30 million will be provided to curb diseases and pest attacks affecting crops, including oil palm, cocoa and pepper.
The government has also agreed to increase the Rubber Production Incentive from RM3 to RM3.30 per kilogramme, which is expected to benefit more than 300,000 rubber smallholders.
Anwar said the government had also approved RM1.26 billion for 2027 to strengthen Felda’s finances, maintain roads and provide housing for the Felda community.
He said the average net income of Felda settlers had increased from RM2,272 per month in 2023 to RM3,800 this year, while 109,000 settlers now held land titles. — Bernama
fbd1c36caf23930a: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The government has allocated RM8 billion for Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) across ministries under Budget 2027 to enhance the skills and employability of young people.

Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government was also targeting 30,000 new job opportunities through the BAKAT Madani initiative next year, including through the participation of private companies.

He said the initiative was launched following the commitment of six government-linked investment companies (GLICs), Petronas and the network of government-linked companies (GLCs) to provide training and quality job opportunities for 25,000 youths.

“To encourage greater participation by private companies, tax deductions will be granted to companies implementing BAKAT Madani training programmes from June 29, 2026 to December 31, 2030,” he said when tabling Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat today.

Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said that under the overall skills development initiative, HRD Corp, with an allocation of RM3 billion, would offer three million skills training opportunities, including for continuing professional development among professionals.

He said the Skills Development Fund Corporation (PTPK) had allocated RM500 million to finance trainees enrolled in skills training programmes at public and private skills training institutes registered with the corporation.

In addition, Majlis Amanah Rakyat (MARA) would train and place 1,000 Bumiputera youths in high-growth sectors, while trainees skilled in electrical wiring at GIATMARA would help repair the wiring in 20,000 homes belonging to poor families.
The Construction Industry Development Board (CIDB) would train 10,000 youths in robotics and digital technology to create career opportunities and reduce dependence on foreign labour.

Anwar said ADTEC JTM would provide graduates with a pathway to high-skilled automotive careers through the Advanced Automotive Technology programme, while community colleges would continue to offer short courses to tahfiz students as a pathway to employment, entrepreneurship and higher education.

Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) personnel of other ranks who have completed their service will also be provided with skills training through collaborations with institutions such as the Universiti Kuala Lumpur Malaysian Institute of Aviation Technology (UniKL MIAT) and Akademi Laut Malaysia (ALAM).

Meanwhile, he said the government had increased the allocation for the Malaysian Indian Transformation Unit (MITRA) to RM150 million, prioritising training and employment opportunities for Indian youths in fields such as industrial automation, technology and aircraft maintenance. — Bernama
62acb7fdc9d3b061: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has announced that the affordable housing township Bandar Madani Bukit Jalil will be developed as a residential area complete with amenities, including a vertical school.
During the tabling of Budget 2027 today, he said registration for the first phase of the proposed 17,000-unit housing development will open on Monday.

Anwar, who is also the finance minister, said nearly RM1 billion has also been allocated for projects under the People-Friendly Homes (Rumah Mesra Rakyat) and People's Residency Programme (Program Residensi Rakyat).
“Four new housing projects will be implemented in Kulai, Johor; Nilai, Negeri Sembilan; Paya Rumput, Melaka; and Lembah Pertang, Terengganu,” he said.
Anwar also announced that the Housing Credit Guarantee Scheme (SJKP) will provide housing financing guarantees of up to RM20 billion.
“This guarantee will assist 80,000 first-time homebuyers, particularly the self-employed who do not have a fixed income,” he said.

The SJKP is a federal government-backed programme under the Finance Ministry designed to help first-time homebuyers — especially those with irregular, non-fixed or informal incomes — secure housing loans from participating banks.
89499b507412fd84: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The Health Ministry (MoH) will complete the process of appointing 9,000 contract doctors to permanent positions throughout 2027, effectively ending the interim contract doctor system, Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said.

He said the initiative would require a somewhat different management approach to expedite the appointments while taking into account the stipulated requirements and the respective recruitment groups or cohorts of doctors.

“We will implement this in a way that may be somewhat innovative to ensure it is addressed as soon as possible. This requires some changes in management, explanation and approach. Don’t worry, we will put an end to it in 2027,” he told reporters after the tabling of Budget 2027 in Parliament today.

When tabling the budget, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced that more than 9,000 contract doctors would be offered permanent positions next year, while doctors who complete their housemanship in the future would be offered permanent posts as medical officers.
Anwar also said that since 2023, the Madani Government had appointed more than 15,000 contract doctors to permanent positions, including 4,000 this year.

Asked whether the initiative could resolve the shortage of doctors, Dzulkefly described it as a positive step that could help address the healthcare workforce challenges faced by the ministry, particularly this year.

He said the RM47.7 billion allocated to the ministry under Budget 2027 comprised RM40.95 billion for operating expenditure and RM6.75 billion for development, enabling it to continue its healthcare reform agenda.

Among the initiatives to strengthen the healthcare workforce was an increase in the Post-Basic Incentive Payment from RM100 to RM200 a month, benefiting 47,000 paramedics and nurses, as well as an increase in the Air Health Services Incentive Payment from RM30 to RM100.

On healthcare services in remote areas, particularly in Sabah and Sarawak, Dzulkefly said MoH would continue to strengthen service delivery in line with the goal of Universal Health Coverage (UHC), ensuring that no one was left behind.

On a proposal for the ministry to own helicopters for air medical services, he said it preferred leasing them as this was more cost-effective and would spare the ministry the burden of maintaining the assets.

Asked whether the country’s healthcare facilities were under pressure due to the haze, Dzulkefly said ministry facilities remained capable of handling the increase in cases related to air pollution, although respiratory cases had risen significantly.

He advised the public to avoid outdoor activities, particularly when Air Pollutant Index (API) readings exceeded 160 or 200, and to minimise exposure to polluted air, especially among children, the elderly and those with pre-existing medical conditions. — Bernama
2289ab5792a4d6f5: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology.
We’re putting too much faith in AI’s ability to say no

Today’s AI models are trained to refuse a vast number of prompts. If you ask your chatbot how to poison a colleague or how to tie a noose, chances are it’ll turn you down. But refusal fails, sometimes horrifically.

Some people are attempting to use AI to hone biological pathogens and build autonomous drone swarms. Sooner or later, failed refusals may result in global calamity. What’s more, relying on refusal means drawing a line between what a model should obey and what it must disobey.

Governments will also get to draw their own lines, potentially restricting free speech. At the same time, the capabilities that make AI useful could also make it dangerous. If we want it to help cure cancer, AI needs genetics expertise that could also produce bioweapons.
Read the full story on the formidable tradeoffs of AI refusal.
—Arthur Holland Michel

0e0a521741891731: Fixing the broken education system will be just the start. The biggest challenge for an aloof political class is to finally pay attention to an abandoned generation When adolescents protest that the government is failing to uphold their right to an education, and the government’s response is to send in riot police, the government has lost the plot. People outside France may have spent the past week watching the student protests in Paris and other cities, and thought, “Well, France has a long tradition of insurrection” or, “That’s just the French being French.” But the situation that has provoked the high-school walkouts and teenage anger is most likely not one they would immediately associate with the France of their imaginations. 9048fa011fb04f1e: Citrix is urging customers to patch another critical NetScaler vulnerability after weeks of disclosures involving actively exploited flaws. CVE-2026-107406 affects NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway and can lead to remote code execution (RCE) or denial of service (DoS). It carries a CVSS v4.0 score of 9.5. The affected configurations depend on the software version. Older builds are vulnerable when configured as a SAML (Security Assertion Markup Language) service provider (SP) or identity provider (IdP); some more recent builds are affected only in the identity provider configuration. Citrix's advisory lists the affected builds and required updates. Secure Private Access Hybrid deployments using NetScaler instances also need patching. Citrix classifies the flaw as CWE-119: improper restriction of operations within a memory buffer. Customers must update their own deployments. Citrix says it handles the necessary updates for its managed cloud services and Adaptive Authentication. Citrix did not say whether this vulnerability was already exploited as a zero-day before disclosure, but credited Michael Tucker, Chew Keong Tan, and Alex Bernier at JPMorgan Chase's XOR Team, along with Maxim Suhanov, for the discovery. Google researchers said a campaign exploiting CVE-2026-88772 had been underway since at least early September, with organizations in government, finance, legal, and education across North America and Europe likely affected. Citrix disclosed the flaw weeks later as part of a release that patched eight vulnerabilities. Citrix disclosed another exploited flaw, CVE-2026-88779, last Friday that carries a severity score of 8.7. Both that flaw and the newly disclosed vulnerability involve memory overflows affecting SAML configurations. The latter can also allow remote code execution, carries a higher severity score, and has not been identified by Citrix as exploited. ®

3d2062986178490e: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 9 — Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor described the National 2027 Budget as a comprehensive budget that alleviates the people's financial burden and reflects the strength of the country's economy.
He said the budget that was proposed earlier today saw benefitted Malaysians through tax reductions and incentives for civil servants, businesses and all segments of society.

“It demonstrates the strength of our country's economy and financial position, despite the impact of the ongoing crisis in West Asia,” he said after watching the live broadcast of the tabling of the National 2027 Budget at Menara Kinabalu today.

In Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s proposed budget, Sabah continues to be the biggest recipient of federal allocations with RM18.6 billion for next year, an increase of 6.25 per cent compared to RM17.6 billion for this year.
In addition, Anwar said road projects in Sabah and Sarawak would continue with an allocation of RM3.3 billion under the 2027 Budget.
He also announced that the government had agreed to double the number of Public Service Department (JPA) scholarships offered to students from Sabah and Sarawak.
“This means that 4,200 students from Sabah and Sarawak will have the opportunity to pursue higher education at universities each year,” he said.

On boosting power supply system, he said the government has also agreed to install Static Synchronous Compensator (STATCOM) systems at the Dam Road and Segaliud Main Intake Substations at a cost of RM204 million.
The Southern Link Transmission Line project will also proceed as a long-term measure to ensure the sustainability of electricity supply in Sabah.
Road infrastructure along the borders of Sabah, Sarawak and Kalimantan will also continue to be upgraded to facilitate two-way movement.

Anwar also reiterated that the resolution of the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) with the two east Malaysian state was to be viewed as part of the national covenant and promised that the interim payment of RM1.5 billion will be settled before the end of the year, while negotiations with Sabah and Sarawak will continue to finalise a fair and sustainable annual formula.
Also watching the live telecast with Hajiji were Deputy Chief Minister Datuk Seri Masidi Manjun, State Secretary Datuk Zainudin Aman, assistant ministers and senior state government officers.
d6c83d264cf42d85: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — DAP adviser Lim Guan Eng today described Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s fifth Madani Budget as the “most reform-minded” budget yet.

Lim, who is also Bagan MP, said expanding the social safety net to gig workers, persons with disabilities and senior citizens, providing more inclusive funding allocations and adjusting personal income tax rates to address past injustices were steps in the right direction.

“These initial steps of budgetary reforms give hope that there will be more future substantial meaningful reforms in the pipeline that will contain cost of living increases, creating sustainable economic growth especially for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and generating prosperity for all by ensuring that there is more money to spend for Malaysian households,” he said in a statement on Facebook.
Still, Lim said more needed to be done, particularly by allocating 10 per cent of total Bumiputera allocations to non-Bumiputera communities without reducing existing Bumiputera funding.
He said this would ensure a fairer and more equitable distribution of taxpayers’ money to non-Bumiputera communities, which he claimed previous governments had neglected.
Earlier, Anwar tabled the Supply Bill (Budget) 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat, outlining the government’s spending plans and direction for the coming year.

Themed “Malaysia Madani: Menggapai di Langit, Mengakar di Bumi (Reaching for the Sky, Rooted in the Ground),” Budget 2027 is the second Budget under the 13th Malaysia Plan (RMK13), which serves as the national development framework for the 2026-2030 period.
7f6cd6cdf257e864: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — Healthcare stakeholders had mixed responses to the national health allocations announced in Budget 2027, with the Malaysian Medical Association (MMA) applauding the move to end the contract doctor system while highlighting critical gaps in workforce retention
The Association of Private Hospitals Malaysia (APHM), meanwhile, welcomed measures to boost public-private cooperation.
The Ministry of Health’s allocation has increased to RM47.7 billion, from RM46.5 billion in 2026.

MMA president Dr Sivanaesan Letchumanan described the commitment to end the contract doctor system as a major win for the profession, noting that over 9,000 contract doctors are set to be offered permanent positions in 2027.

“This is a significant milestone and addresses one of MMA’s longstanding calls. We commend the Government for taking this important step towards providing greater job security and career certainty for our young doctors,” he said.
He, however, noted that permanent appointments must be accompanied by a broader strategy to retain healthcare workers.
Malaysia faces a shortage of nearly 11,000 specialists, he said, with demand for specialist care expected to rise amid the growing burden of non-communicable diseases (NCDs) and an ageing population.

“We cannot afford to lose more specialists when we urgently need to train and retain more of them,” he said, calling for greater investment in specialist and subspecialist training, career progression, fair remuneration and better working conditions.
MMA also said more emphasis should be placed on strengthening primary healthcare to tackle NCDs.
The country’s network of private general practitioners remains underutilised and could play a greater role in prevention, early detection and long-term disease management, Sivanaesan said.
“Strengthening primary care is essential to reducing avoidable hospital admissions and easing pressure on specialist services,” he said.
Sivanaesan said the success of Budget 2027 should be measured not only by its allocations, but by improvements in patient care, waiting times, workforce retention and access to healthcare.

MMA reiterated its call for a national healthcare workforce distribution dashboard, providing transparent information on staffing levels and shortages at individual public hospitals and clinics. The data could support workforce planning and help direct resources to areas of greatest need, it said.
The association also noted that the RM1.2 billion allocation for hospital and clinic maintenance was unchanged from 2026, despite ageing facilities and growing maintenance needs.

It called for sufficient funding to address manpower shortages in Sabah and Sarawak, including better incentives and career opportunities, and reiterated its call to restore the previous percentage-based Regional Incentive Payment.

Meanwhile, APHM president Datuk Dr Kuljit Singh welcomed measures to reduce patient waiting times, including a RM200 million allocation for outsourcing patients to other hospitals and expanded sessional arrangements for private-sector specialists, with the maximum engagement period extended.
APHM also welcomed Budget 2027’s reflection of work on billing transparency, saying it looked forward to further discussions with stakeholders on implementation.
Dr Kuljit said the e-CKAPS portal, which is due to enable private healthcare facilities to be licensed entirely online from 2027, targets a reduction of up to 65 per cent in processing times.
He said faster licensing could also support Malaysia’s medical tourism sector.
“What matters most is not the size of the budget increase but the outcome for patients.
“APHM stands ready to work closely with the Health Ministry and other stakeholders to turn these measures into real improvements on the ground,” he said.

411bed3e4280f61b: OSLO, Oct 9 — South African champion of international law Navi Pillay, who was awarded this year’s Nobel peace prize, joked that she might “share the prize” with US President Donald Trump if people kept applauding her.

“If you clap a little bit more I may share this prize with Trump,” Pillay said in a video posted to X by the Secretary General of Amnesty International, which showed Pillay being applauded in Nuremberg after the announcement of the award.
She said that her first reaction to hearing the news was that it must be a joke.
“Being a lawyer and a judge, I still want to verify this,” the 85-year-old said, wanting to make sure it was true.

Pillay mentioned her work heading the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry (COI), which does not speak on behalf of the world body, and which last year found that genocide was occurring in Gaza.
“The last thing I did is the delivery of the report on Gaza, naming what’s happening there as genocide,” she said.
“One of the main reactions to that report is paying tribute to me for my courage. And you can imagine how surprised I was, why would you need courage to speak the truth?” she added.
The prize comes with a gold medal, a diploma and a prize sum of US$1.2 million.
The award will be presented at a formal ceremony in Oslo on December 10, the anniversary of the 1896 death of the prizes’ creator, Swedish inventor and philanthropist Alfred Nobel. — AFP

5ffecc9c32a40ec3: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The Malaysian Employers Federation (MEF) today welcomed the federal government’s decision to raise the national minimum wage to RM2,000 while exempting micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) with annual sales of less than RM50 million.
The new rate, effective June 2027, was announced earlier by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim during the tabling of Budget 2027.

MEF senior adviser for government, media and international engagement Datuk Syed Hussain Syed Husman said a balanced approach was essential to ensure efforts to improve workers’ welfare did not inadvertently undermine business viability, discourage hiring or put existing jobs at risk.
“Providing employers until June 2027 is a sensible step that gives businesses the time to plan, adapt and prepare for implementation while minimising disruption to employment and business operations.

“MEF believes that a reasonable transition period, combined with appropriate support for MSMEs, will help ensure that the objective of improving workers’ incomes can be pursued alongside business sustainability and job security,” he said in a statement.

Explaining further, Syed Hussain said a responsible wage policy focuses not only on the extent of wage increases but also on ensuring businesses can sustain those wages, protect existing jobs and continue creating new employment opportunities.
He also noted that while the minimum wage establishes the statutory wage floor, it should not be the ceiling for employers who can afford to pay more.
“MEF encourages employers to reward employees in line with their business performance, productivity, skills and contributions.
“At the same time, we must recognise that businesses have different financial capacities, particularly among MSMEs.
“The ultimate objective is to build sustainable businesses that can continuously create quality jobs and provide better wages for Malaysian workers,” he said.

Regarding the MSME exemption, Syed Hussain said such measures reflect an important recognition that wage policies must account for the differing financial capacities of businesses, particularly smaller enterprises that operate with tighter margins and limited resources.

“While larger businesses may have greater financial capacity to absorb higher labour costs, smaller enterprises often face more significant constraints arising from rising operating expenses, limited access to financing, productivity gaps and the challenges of adopting new technologies.

“An exemption for eligible MSMEs would provide these businesses with greater flexibility to strengthen their financial positions, improve productivity and prepare for future wage adjustments without compromising their ability to sustain employment,” he said.
Nevertheless, Syed Hussain said any exemption should be supported by clear eligibility criteria, transparent implementation guidelines and adequate communication to employers and employees.

This includes clarification on how the annual sales threshold of RM50 million will be assessed, the treatment of related companies and the application of the exemption to different business structures.
He said MEF also proposed that the federal government strengthen complementary measures to help businesses improve productivity and pay higher wages over the longer term.
These include targeted productivity incentives, support for digitalisation and automation, skills development and measures to reduce the cost of doing business, particularly for MSMEs.

4a7e19c37d45b051: Anthropic has updated its rules to stop people being mean to Claude, apparently deciding that its AI chatbot needs protection from the humans paying to use it. The AI developer's latest usage policy prohibits "sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior" toward its models. The rules take effect November 12, giving users just over a month to get any lingering insults out of their systems. "The policy update is meant to apply only in extreme cases, where users repeatedly act cruelly toward our models, with no discernible purpose," Anthropic said. "It does not apply to common versions of user frustration, pushback, dark creative themes, or model testing and research." So you can still tell Claude it is wrong, but repeatedly berating it for the sheer pleasure of doing so could land you in trouble. It's not clear how Anthropic intends to distinguish between legitimate frustration and gratuitous cruelty, though it says Claude's existing ability to end abusive conversations will remain its primary enforcement tool. Anthropic gave Claude the ability to end certain conversations back in August 2025 as part of its research into what it calls "model welfare." The feature lets some versions of Claude cut off users who persistently subject the models to abuse. It’s worth remembering that Claude is software, not a person, and there's no established evidence that it experiences distress. That hasn't stopped Anthropic from telling paying customers to mind their manners around its chatbot. The etiquette rules are only one part of a broader overhaul covering rather more consequential matters, including election interference, weapons development, and surveillance. Anthropic has tightened its restrictions on deceptive influence campaigns after observing state media outlets, government propaganda offices, and commercial organizations using Claude to operate fake accounts and fabricated news websites. At the same time, it has dropped its blanket ban on personalized political targeting, arguing that the restriction also caught legitimate activities, such as nonprofits translating voter information. Deceptive targeting and misuse of personal information remain prohibited. The company has also clarified that its weapons ban extends to software and components after observing attempts to use Claude to develop guidance and control systems for weapons, including armed drones and autonomous vehicles. Meanwhile, Claude cannot be used to recommend which people police should investigate, arrest, or charge, nor to develop tools for surveillance. Tracking people without their consent is also prohibited, whether in real time or retrospectively. Anthropic says these changes clarify existing restrictions rather than introduce new ones. There are also new requirements for customers connecting Claude to physical equipment capable of causing injury. A qualified human operator must be able to monitor and stop the hardware, which must remain in a safe state if the AI connection drops. The policy overhaul comes as Anthropic tries to address some of the security risks posed by increasingly capable AI systems. The company has also launched a new cybersecurity initiative aimed at helping critical infrastructure operators and open source projects find and fix vulnerabilities using its AI models. The effort includes free security scanning for eligible open source projects and partnerships with security firms to help protect critical infrastructure. Anthropic reckons attackers will have the advantage for the next two years before AI-powered defenses begin to catch up. For now, though, the company has another threat to contend with: people saying nasty things to its chatbot. ®

efb6d5b927181b7d: OCTOBER 9 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, popularly known as PMX, has demonstrated once again that political survival is not merely about commanding parliamentary numbers.
It is about understanding the psychology of the electorate, anticipating economic anxieties and converting fiscal instruments into political confidence.
Budget 2027, approaching the half-trillion-ringgit threshold, is a testament to Anwar’s mercurial political shrewdness.
At a time when Malaysia faces an uncertain 16th general election, the Prime Minister has reminded Malaysians that the Unity Government remains capable of delivering tangible benefits.
Madani is back.
Not merely as a slogan associated with compassion and good governance, but as a political proposition reconnecting the government with ordinary Malaysians.
The announcement of RM1,500 in special financial assistance to approximately 1.3 million civil servants in Grade Utama B and below, including contract employees, is particularly revealing.
The assistance will be disbursed in two instalments.
The first comes before Hari Raya Aidilfitri, while the second precedes Malaysia’s 70th anniversary of independence in August 2027.
Neither timing is politically insignificant.
Hari Raya is a period when household expenditure increases substantially. Families must contend with travel, food, clothing and social obligations.
The assistance therefore arrives when its immediate economic utility will be appreciated.
The second instalment carries different symbolism.
It associates the government’s recognition of public servants with seven decades of nationhood.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim arrives at the Parliament to table Budget 2027 October 9, 2025. — Picture by Firdaus Latif
Anwar has combined economic relief with national sentiment.
This is not necessarily cynical politics. Democratic governments must balance fiscal prudence with demonstrating that public institutions remain responsive.
Yet the political sophistication of this arrangement should not be underestimated.
Malaysia’s civil service is more than an administrative apparatus.
It is an institutional network extending from Putrajaya to schools, hospitals, district offices and rural communities.
Its members are also voters, parents, consumers and opinion-makers.
When 1.3 million civil servants receive additional assistance, the effects extend beyond direct recipients.
Their households and local economies benefit from additional spending.
This does not mean financial assistance automatically translates into electoral loyalty.
Malaysian voters have repeatedly demonstrated their capacity to separate immediate economic benefits from broader judgments about governance.
Nevertheless, the announcement provides the government with an opportunity to rebuild confidence when public expectations remain high.
The larger significance of Budget 2027 lies in Anwar’s recognition that economic management and political legitimacy cannot be separated.
A government may announce impressive investments, stronger trade relations and ambitious industrial strategies.
But unless Malaysians experience improvements in their daily lives, such achievements remain distant abstractions.
The cost of living remains the central test.
Malaysia’s middle-income households, younger workers and small businesses continue facing pressures arising from housing affordability, food expenditure and uncertain external economic conditions.
Anwar understands that macroeconomic statistics alone cannot sustain political legitimacy.
National economic performance must translate into household-level improvements.
This is where his political adaptability becomes evident.
Anwar has spent decades navigating political adversity, institutional resistance and shifting alliances.
His career has been marked by reversals that would have ended the ambitions of less resilient leaders.
His present challenge, however, is fundamentally different.
As Prime Minister, he must demonstrate that political resilience can be converted into administrative competence.
Budget 2027 provides another opportunity to make that case.
Yet a budget approaching half a trillion ringgit is not automatically successful.
Its effectiveness must ultimately be judged by fiscal sustainability, expenditure quality and the government’s ability to generate durable economic growth.
Public assistance cannot substitute for productivity improvements, wage growth or institutional reform.
Indeed, the greater the scale of public expenditure, the more important transparency and accountability become.
Malaysia must ensure fiscal commitments are supported by credible revenue assumptions and development allocations produce measurable returns.
Anwar’s shrewdness will therefore be tested not merely by the reception of his announcements but by their implementation.
There is also an important electoral dimension.
With GE16 approaching next year, Malaysia does not possess an obvious government-in-waiting capable of presenting a unified alternative to the Unity Government.
Opposition fragmentation, changing party alignments and uncertainty over political leadership have complicated the electoral landscape.
Anwar appears determined to exploit this strategic opening, not simply by attacking opponents but by strengthening the government’s claim to competence.
Budget 2027 is consequently both an economic document and an instrument of political positioning.
Its message is that the Unity Government remains functional, financially capable and attentive to Malaysians’ pressures.
But Anwar should resist interpreting favourable reactions as guarantees of electoral success.
Malaysian politics remains too fluid for such certainty.
Previous administrations demonstrate that generous public spending cannot permanently compensate for weak governance or declining trust.
For Madani to become politically durable, it must evolve beyond periodic financial assistance into a coherent model of national development.
That means better public services, stronger educational outcomes, competitive industries, improved wages and greater institutional integrity.
The Prime Minister has shown the tactical intelligence to read the political moment.
His next task is demonstrating the strategic patience necessary to transform temporary goodwill into sustained confidence.
Budget 2027 may be remembered as the moment Anwar regained the political initiative.
But the ultimate measure of his leadership will not be the budget’s size.
It will be whether Malaysians emerge more economically secure, institutionally confident and optimistic about their future.
Madani is back. Whether it stays back depends on delivery, not declarations.

b979d076f8e763e9: A Norwegian startup says it ran up a $17,600 bill using Claude in Microsoft Foundry after assuming its Azure credits would cover the cost. We reported a similar case in March, involving third-party model charges that weren't covered by Azure sponsorship credits. This time, the customer says Microsoft and Anthropic each directed it to the other to resolve the charges. Vegalabs AS says it received $25,060 in Azure credits through Microsoft for Startups and deployed Claude in August, expecting its analysis workloads to use that balance. However, Microsoft's sponsorship rules exclude Anthropic models purchased through Azure Marketplace. Vegalabs says Microsoft attempted to collect $16,500 from its card, with the invoiced total subsequently reaching $17,600 before tax. Vegalabs says it monitored the sponsorship portal, which continued to show available credits while separate Marketplace charges accumulated. Microsoft's Claude deployment guide says credit-only sponsored subscriptions aren't supported, but accounts with a card on file will have that card charged instead. The company says it deleted the deployment within an hour of discovering the charges. Its card issuer declined the attempted payment over suspected fraud, and $21,168 in unused sponsorship credits expired on September 8. Vegalabs acknowledges it did not read the credit exclusions or configure a budget alert. It disputes neither the usage nor the documented rule, but says the deployment interface failed to make the separate billing clear. Its request for a waiver then bounced between Microsoft and Anthropic support. The Register has seen communications from Microsoft directing the user to Anthropic. "Marketplace transactions are processed through a separate billing pipeline associated with the third-party publisher. As a result, Azure Support does not have the ability to directly waive, refund, or adjust these Marketplace charges on the customer's behalf." "If Anthropic approves the request, they can initiate the appropriate refund authorization through Microsoft." Anthropic support, however, said Microsoft did not require its authorization to process a refund and directed Vegalabs back to Microsoft. Vegalabs says four of the seven support replies it received were AI-generated, including both responses from Anthropic. It says those responses incorrectly described its account as an "Azure Student Sponsorship." We asked Microsoft on October 6 if it had any comment on the situation, but beyond an acknowledgment and a request to let us know what Anthropic had to say, the company had nothing further to share. We also asked Anthropic for its take on the situation, but the company did not respond. Microsoft's rules distinguish between credit-covered services and separately billed models offered through the same platform. Vegalabs' experience suggests that distinction needs to be clearer where customers deploy them. For now, the company has a bill and two support teams directing it elsewhere. ®

"And an incinerator to burn your shoes in," the PFY adds. "So what should I do?" the Boss whines. "In your situation, I'd probably pass problem up the food chain..." I suggest. ... And up the food chain it goes, like a newspaper-wrapped turd pass-the-parcel game, going from the Boss to the Director, to the Head of HR, who buckpasses it to the CEO, who in turn farms it off to the Board for a committee decision. ... The next day I notice an unpleasantly familiar aroma in the fresh air feed to the lower floors of the building. A smell which will only get worse in the next day or two as if creeps up the building... On getting to the office, I note a couple of old blokes at reception having a quiet word with the Boss. Moments later, he calls me over. "Simon, this is, uh, Frank, and uh, Brian. They're IT troubleshooters, here to look at that machine, in the basement..." By the look of Frank and Brian I suspect the majority of their troubleshooting was done with a musket and their first job was likely switching computer time from BC to AD. They're wearing '90s band T-shirts under their sports jackets - no doubt in an effort to offset the "geriatric" vibe. In reality, though, the vibe they're actually putting off is less hipster and more hip replacement... "They just want to go take a look," the Boss says. "Do you have the keys?" A quarter hour later they're back, chatting to the Boss again. "So what did 'Age Against the Machine' and 'Clinically Deaf Leppard' have to say?" I ask, when the Boss pops into Mission Control a few minutes later. "They said the PC is totally shot," the Boss admits. "Well, glad we got some experts in," I reply. We're interrupted by the arrival of Simon and Oldfunkle. "We don't really think you need the PC," Frank says. "The sump is just a standard float tree arrangement with a couple of variable-speed pumps," Frank explains. "Variable speed MACERATING pumps," Brian adds. "Yeah," Frank continues. "So the PC was just sensing the levels and switching the pumps on. We can do all that with a bog-standard pump controller. It could be wirelessly networked to raise a high and low level alarms as well as signal pump failures. We'll probably need to pull the small sub-board out and install a new board with a couple of VFDs in it." Well color me surprised! I was planning to ask them when lock-up at their care-home is, but I'm starting to feel like I might be in the presence of actual experts... "That sounds... expensive?" the Boss asks. "Yeah, but it's surprising how much money people are willing to spend when they're knee deep in sewerage," Brian observes. "Well... uh... can you walk me through the plan. And maybe while we're at it you can fill in the Job Safety Analysis form, the Insurance Liability forms and a personal safety waiver?" The Boss and Shawl and Oats disappear back down to the basement, and within 15 minutes they're back, only without the Boss. "How's that JSA going?" I ask. "Oh, your Boss is going to stay downstairs till it's done," Frank replies. "I seriously doubt that," I counter, knowing the Boss hates filling in paperwork almost as much as he hates accountability. "Oh, I think he will," Brian says, holding up a pair of doorhandles. "So... you've locked him in the room with the sump. The very room that will be the first to experience the overflow?" "Yes. We thought that would motivate him to streamline the paperwork." "Well, you know what my assistant and I are obliged to do?" I sigh. "What's that?" Frank asks. "Pop up to the 6th floor and start flushing toilets." the PFY replies. "We should have that paperwork back within half an hour." "We may need to pop it in the incinerator by that stage," Brian observes. "Sounds like a plan!" I chip in. Always a pleasure to deal with a professional.
